This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed being aggrieved by the impugned award passed in MCC No.34/2016 by the Member of Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Sehor vide order dated 06.05.2017 by which the appellants filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 was dismissed on the ground that the claimant failed to prove that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle MP-09-CP-6912.
2.

The facts giving rise to the claim petition in nutshell are that on 21.06.2013 the deceased Sadab with his friend chandu was returning from Bhowkhedi on his motorcycle, when they reached near Paliwal Nursery on Ichhawar Sehor Road.
The driver of the vehicle MP-09-CP-6912 driving the car rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle of the deceased from the backside as a result Sadab and his friend fell down.

Thereafter, deceased Sadab was brought to the Government Hospital Sehore after first aid he was referred to Bhopal and family members admitted the deceased in LBS Hospital,
Bhopal during the treatment on 22.06.2015 deceased died.
FIR was registered against the respondent No.1 as Crime No.337/2015 at the Police Station Ichhawar.

The charge sheet was filed against the respondent No.1.
3.
The claimants asserting that the deceased was 28 years of age and was doing the business of Hatchery and selling of the eggs and chicken and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The claimants mother, wife and parents have suffered economic loss and loss of dependency, hence, filed the claim petition.

4. On the petition, the owner/driver of the vehicle filing the reply of the petition denied the involvement of the car and the negligence and pleaded that in the case the accident is proved the Insurance Company is liable to compensate the claimants.

5. The Insurance Company has denied the whole incident and had defended the claim on the ground that FIR was falsely lodged after one month and thirteen days with the collusion of the police authorities, the vehicle No.MP- 09-CP-6912 was not involved in the accident.
On the false grounds the claim has been filed.
The Insurance Company is not liable to compensate the damages suffered by the Claimants as the car was being driven in the violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance policy.

2 6. The Claim Tribunal framed the issues and after recording the evidence of the parties has dismissed the claim petition.
7 .

Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the claim Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition only on the entry mentioned in the Ex.P-14 but the deceased has not given the history that he suffered the injury by his own act and Police has lodged the FIR and after investigation charge sheeted the respondent No.1 and the independent witness Anwar Kha (PW-2) has clearly stated that he was the eye witness but the Claim Tribunal has dismissed the claim also on the ground that the claimants have not examined Chandu who was on the motorcycle in which the deceased was travelling and the FIR was not lodged in the time.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants has also submitted that the owner/the driver of the car has not examined himself and Insurance Company has not produced any evidence to prove their defence that the vehicle was falsely implicated in the case but Claim Tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim only on the technical grounds.
9. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of Insurance Company has submitted that the claim Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence, as in the discharge card (Ex.P-14) the hospital authorities have clearly mentioned that on the date of incident 21.6.2015 at 7:30 PM bike skid and as a result the deceased suffered the injuries and ultimately died and that is the reason the FIR was not lodged against any person but after a long delay on 02.08.2015 the FIR was lodged.
Chandu was the best witness but that was not examined, hence, the claim tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim.
10. I have gone through the record, it is not disputed that deceased Sadab son of Abdul Sattar suffered injuries in the vehicular accident.

Further more, this fact is supported by the statement of Anwar Kha (PW-2) and he has clearly stated that the deceased was traveling in the motorcycle and the offending vehicle hit the motorcycle and as a result the deceased Sadab and Chandu were thrown away from the motorcycle and Sadab suffered injury over the head.

11. This fact is further supported by the MLC report of LBS Hospital, Bhopal (Ex.P-13) in which the hospital authority has sent the information to the Police Station on 21.06.2015 and clearly mentioned that on 21.06.2015 at 7:30 PM the injured Sadab suffered injury in Ichhawar-Sehore road in a road traffic accident and primary treatment was provided in Sehore Hospital where the he was unconscious and as per Ex.P-14 the deceased suffered the head injury.
On 22.06.2015 at 10:30 AM deceased died.

The Police Station Shahjahanabad registered Merg Intimation on the information of Dr. Ashish Verm (Ex.P-4) and in that it is clearly mentioned that in Ichhawar Sehore Road the deceased met with vehicular accident and he was admitted on 21.06.2015 in LBS Hospital,
Bhopal and on 22.06.2015 at 10:30 AM expired and as per Ex.P-9 and Ex.P-10 application for the postmortem and Postmortem report, deceased died due to shock and hemorrhage and that was due to head injury.

12. Thus, it is crystal and clear that the deceased met with the vehicular accident on 21.06.2015 on 7:30 PM near Ichhawar Sehore Road and as a result of the injuries suffered in the accident, he died.

Asma Bee vs Younish Mohd. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142525531/
3 13.

The Claim Tribunal has basically dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the motorcycle of the deceased was not recovered from the place of incident and Anwar (PW-2) has not passed the information to the Police Authorities and he has not admitted the deceased to the Hospital and the Police registered the FIR after a month and Anwar has not lodged any FIR.

14. On this point, the case of Sunita and Ors. vs Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and Ors., AIR 2019 SC 994 , the Apex Court has held that "Tribunal stricto sensu is not bound by the pleading of the parties and its function is to determine the amount of fair compensation, claimants are merely to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt cannot be applied by Tribunal dealing with the motor accident claim cases.

entities.text: Sunita and Ors. vs Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and Ors., AIR 2019 SC 994
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court has clearly held that by not examining the pillion rider the claim cannot be dismissed and there is no provision in the Motor Vehicle Act to preclude the claimant to citing a witness who has not been named as a witness in the list of the criminal case."

15. On the above basis if witness Asma Bee (AW-1) has clearly stated that deceased was her husband and on that date he went to sell garlic and opinion in the Ichhawar market and after selling he was returning and accident happened near Paliwal Nursery.

She has exhibited the papers of the criminal case from Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-15 but in the cross examination she has clearly admitted that she was not present on the spot and on the information of other, she came to know that her husband has sustained the injury in an accident.
She has further stated in para-9 that her brother-in-law told her that Chandu was with her husband at the time of accident.
She has further stated that Chandu has also suffered injuries.

16. The Witness Anwar (AW-2) has stated that on the date of incident he was returning from Ichhawar to Sehor at 6:45-7:00 PM and when he reached near Paliwal Nursery, he saw that Sadab and Chandu were going towards Ichhawar, at that time a white coloured car bearing registration No.MP-09-CP- 6912 hit the motorcycle of Sadab from backside as a result Sadab and Chandu were thrown away from motorcycle and Sadab suffered injuries on his head.
He called the Ambulance by dialing 108, after 10 minutes the Ambulance reached there and Sadab was brought to Government Hospital, Sehore from where he was referred to LBS Hospital, Bhopal.
17. In the cross examination by respondent No.1 nothing has been brought on record that this witness was not present on the spot.
In the cross examination of the Insurance Company, he has clearly stated that he has disclosed the vehicle number to the SHO of Police Station- Ichhawar and after a month he was called by the Police.

He has also clearly stated in para-7 of the cross examination that Police has recorded his statement in the Police Station and he has denied the fact that due to relation he is supporting the claim of applicant, he has also clearly denied that no such incident has happened.

18. On the point of accident, driver Yunush Mohd. respondent No.1 was the best witness who can explain in which circumstances the accident had happened and whether his vehicle was involved or not and on the date of accident where his vehicle was parked on was on road, but the owner has not examined himself.

Asma Bee vs Younish Mohd. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142525531/
4 19.
The Insurance Company has not examined any witness to rebut the fact that the car was not involved in the vehicular accident.

20. On the point that Chandu was not examined, Anwar (AW-1) is equally important as his name is clearly mentioned as the eye witness Ex.P-1 and it is to worth mentioned that the merg intimation (Ex.P-4) was registered by Police Station Shahjahanabad on 22.06.2015 and this information was passed and Police Station Ichhawar registered the merg intimation on 23.07.2015 and after the inquiry the Police Station has registered the criminal case on 02.08.2015, thus information of the incident and death of deceased in the vehicular accident was in the knowledge of the police authorities and if they have delayed in the inquiry and registering the case, no fault can be found with the LRs of deceased.
21.

Another important factor is that Anwar (PW-2) has not only stated the vehicle number but also stated the vehicle was of white colour and seizure memo (Ex.P-6) the colour of the vehicle has been mentioned as white and in mechanical examination report (Ex.P-8) in the front Bumper, scratches were found.
22.

The MLC (Ex.P-13) was also sent by the LBS Hospital, Bhopal but in that only alleged RTA on 21.06.2015 at 7:30 PM near Ichhawar, Sehore road has been written and it has been clearly written that the injured was unconscious and after death the information sent to the Police Authorities (Ex.P-14) the bike skid has been mentioned but bike skid due to self or any other reason, it has not been mentioned.

Thus, on that note the fact stated in the document without any formal proof cannot be accepted as to be truth as no source of the information has been written in that and it has stated only on the basis of the pillion rider has not been examined by the claimant, the claim petition cannot be thrown away.
On the ground that the FIR was lodged delay, the claim cannot be rejected.

23. Thus, from the above discussion, it is clear that claimant proved that on 21.06.2015 at about 7:00-7:15 PM, the respondent No.1 driving the vehicle rash and negligent manner dashed the motorcycle of the deceased from backside as a result the deceased suffered injuries and died.

24. The issue Nos.2 and 3 regarding the violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy, the Insurance Company has not adduced any evidence and this fact is not proved.
25.

On the point that the deceased was also liable for the accident as discussed above, it is clear that respondents has not adduced any evidence and from the cross examination of the appellant witness it has not been proved that the deceased was also liable for the accident.
Hence, no case of the contributory negligence is made out.
26. Thus, as discussed, the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 and LRs suffered loss of dependency, care and protection and loss of estate.
27. To determine the quantum of compensation, the age, income and number of the dependent are the primary factors.

Asma Bee vs Younish Mohd. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142525531/
5 28.

In this case though the claimants has not produced any document regarding the age of the deceased and in papers of the treatment Ex.P-13, P-14 and P-15 the age of the deceased has been mentioned 28 years and in the postmortem report Ex.P-9 and P-10, 28 years age is mentioned.
Age of the wife is 26 years and the elder daughter's age of the deceased is 9 years.

In the cross examination the claimant Asma Bee in para-8 has stated that her marriage took place at 12 years ago and at that time her age was 15 to 16 years but has admitted that her husband was three years elder to her.
Anwar Kha (PW-2) in para -5 of the cross examination has stated that the deceased marriage took place in the year 1994 and he was at that time 19 to 20 years old.
On that basis, on the date of incident deceased age comes to 40 years but from the evidence of the claimants, it comes to near about 30 years.
On that basis in the documents as mentioned above the age of deceased comes within 25 to 30 age group.
29. In the claim petition the claimants have stated that deceased was having Hatchery and selling the eggs and chicken.
In the chief examination they have exhibited the receipts of selling the Garlic and Onion and that also after the accident.
Thus no document has been produced regarding the business of Hatchery and selling and buying the eggs and chicken.

Thus, evidence is against the pleadings and no evidence has produced to support the pleadings, on that basis it cannot be inferred that deceased was running Hatchery or selling eggs and chicken regularly.
So the income may be assessed on the basis of minimum wages payable to an unskilled labourer and on that time minimum wages applicable to unskilled labourer to Rs.6239/-.
Thus income of the deceased is decided Rs.6239/- monthly.
30. Looking to the age of the deceased as he was labourer, 40% of the income shall be added in the future prospect.
On that basis 6239x40 = 2495.6 @ 2496 shall be added in the head of future prospect total monthly income will come Rs.8735.
Number of dependents are 5, hence, 1/4th of the income shall be deducted in the head of living and personal expenses which comes to Rs.2183.75 @Rs.2184 shall be deducted in that head.

In the age group of deceased being 25 to 30, the multiplier of 17 will be applicable and on that basis the loss of dependency will be Rs.6551x12x17=
Rs.13,36,404/-.
31.

As per judgment of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, AIR 2017 SC 5157 and the principles laid down in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram, 2018 ACJ 2782, the wife/appellant No.1 is entitled for the Rs.44,000/- for loss of spousal consortium and each of claimant Nos.3 to 5 are entitled of Rs.44,000/- for the loss of parental consortium, thus on the head of loss of consortium the claimants are entitled an amount of Rs.1,76,000/-.
32.

33.
Thus claimants are entitled of Rs.15,43,649/- and claimants are also entitled simple interest @7% per annum from 5.03.2016 till the amount is deposited before the Claim Tribunal.

6 34.

Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation amount to the claimants and vehicle was insured with respondent No.2, hence, the Insurance Company is liable to deposit the claim amount before the Claim Tribunal.

35. On the Claim amount being deposited 25% of the Claim amount shall be payable to the wife of the deceased/appellant No.1 and 15% of the claim amount shall be payable to the appellant No.2 mother of deceased.
Rest of the amount shall equally payable to appellant Nos.3 to 5/children of the deceased.

While disbursing the amount, the Claim Tribunal shall following the direction laid down in the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Kerla State Road Transport Corporation vs.
Susamma Thomas, (1994) 2 SCC 176.
